speaker: dobbin
text: They say the foreman never walked out of the Forge. My brothers were chained by him. I won't weep.

speaker: tamsin
text: Oh, pet. I heard the old horn in my sleep last night. Somebody swore the Warden's oath. Was that you?

speaker: tamsin
text: Somebody swore to guard each other in that vault, pet. Not the town, each other. That's the oath that holds.

speaker: tamsin
text: The old Warden's gauntlet is gone from the vault, I hear. Well. Everything is for sale in the end. Not everything, pet.

speaker: osric
text: You carry shadows, child. Hold still... There. The Temple has lifted what clung to you.

speaker: marga
text: On the house, love.

speaker: malthrax
text: You think I came alone? WAKE, GORVAX!

speaker: malthrax
text: Five moons, Emberhollow.

speaker: narrator
text: Gorvax the Tyrant falls! The Blackspire's lights go dark.

speaker: narrator
text: The Blackspire is dark. Princess Elowen is home, and Emberhollow is free. Arise, Knight of the Dawn.

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere far below, a sixth seal stirs. And Malthrax's staff was never found…

speaker: narrator
text: Torchlight gutters on the stair below. Something vast breathes in the dark, and it says your names. Skarn was only the doorman.

speaker: pip
text: You SOLD a SPOON? I need a moment.

speaker: narrator
text: The camp is quiet. Too quiet.

speaker: pip
text: The prophecy is REAL!

speaker: pip
text: Two! Two clues!

speaker: pip
text: Three is a pattern. Patterns are destiny.

speaker: pip
text: Four... I may cry.

speaker: pip
text: FIVE. To the armory!

speaker: vexrath
text: My clan's honour... restored. I will carry this to the throne myself.

speaker: zizzy
text: Oh, we are SO using this on the gate.

speaker: narrator
text: You cut a bound town guard free. "Captain Rowan sent you? Bless you!"

speaker: narrator
text: Lore tablet: "Emberhollow was founded on a sealed tower. The founders buried it, built an inn on top, and agreed never to mention it again."

speaker: narrator
text: Spoon clue 1: a spoon scratched into the wall, pointing down. "THE KEEPERS SLEEP BENEATH." Pip trembles with joy.

speaker: narrator
text: A fresh tunnel, dug straight up toward the Boar & Spoon cellar. You kick out the supports and it caves in. Marga will want to hear.

speaker: narrator
text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 1: "Down in the Warrens where the rat-kings sup, / Grumsh drew his axe and the rats gave up!"

speaker: narrator
text: Dwarven boot-prints, and a hammer-shaped dent in a rat. "That's Mum's hammer," Brambur whispers. "Someone took it deeper."

speaker: narrator
text: The ceiling here sags over a side-passage where you hear cultists chanting. One good pull would bring it down on them, or on you.

speaker: narrator
text: CRACK! The ceiling caves in on the cultist side-passage. Silence, and a pouch of 40 gp rolls out of the dust.

speaker: narrator
text: A torn spellbook page, covered in Fizzwick's tiny handwriting ("NOTE TO SELF: COUNTERSPELL. ALWAYS COUNTERSPELL.").

speaker: narrator
text: Spoon clue 2: a tarnished teaspoon tied to a stalactite with a ribbon marked "II". Pip pockets it reverently.

speaker: narrator
text: Half-sunk in the grotto: a satchel stitched with the royal sun. Elowen's temple relics, still dry inside. Brother Osric will want this.

speaker: narrator
text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 2: "In the Grotto deep where the waters sing, / a lizard with a club tail met a better thing!"

speaker: narrator
text: Tall tale 1: "The staff was carved from a lightning-struck spire," Nettle writes. "Everyone agrees. Nobody saw it."

speaker: narrator
text: Lore tablet: "The First Warden bound the Tyrant-lizard Gorvax beneath the vault with five seals and a very large horn."

speaker: narrator
text: You shatter a humming crystal pylon. Stored dawn-light spills out and sinks into the floor, heading deeper.

speaker: narrator
text: Spoon clue 3: crystal etchings of five spoons in a circle. One is a ladle. "That's cheating," says Pip.

speaker: narrator
text: A crystal-sealed royal decree. The ORIGINAL. It does not exile Vexrath's clan; it knights them.

speaker: narrator
text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 3: "Through Glimmerdeep's glow where the toadstools scream, / Grumsh screamed louder (it was quite the scene)!"

speaker: narrator
text: Tall tale 2: "It hums when he lies," Nettle notes. "So it hums constantly."

speaker: narrator
text: Lore tablet: "Glimmerdeep crystals drink light. Shatter them and the light they hoarded is set free."

speaker: narrator
text: You smash the chains of a captive smith. "Tell Dobbin we're coming home, and we'll be at the vault when you need us."

speaker: narrator
text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. Zizzy's eyes light up. "Oh, we are SO using this on the gate."

speaker: narrator
text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. It looks like the sort of thing a sorcerer would enjoy.

speaker: narrator
text: Spoon clue 4: an anvil stamped with a spoon. Under it, a riddle: "Where the Tyrant sleeps, the silver keeps."

speaker: narrator
text: Zizzy packs the powder against the Ashforge gate. KA-BOOM! The gate, and its guards, are no longer a problem.

speaker: narrator
text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 4: "In Ashforge's heat where the anvils ring, / Grumsh rang louder, being Grumsh, the king!"

speaker: narrator
text: Tall tale 3: "A smith says the staff has a crack near the crystal, mended with cultist spit."

speaker: narrator
text: Lore tablet: "Ashforge was a dwarven forge-hall until Brakk sold it, and its smiths, to the Sovereign."

speaker: narrator
text: Old Tamsin's tale was true. You will sound it when the Tyrant rises.

speaker: narrator
text: Spoon clue 5: the final clue, a spoon-shaped keyhole in the vault wall. Pip hums the Spoon-Keepers' anthem.

speaker: narrator
text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 5: "In the Blackspire vault where the Tyrant lay, / [Grumsh: 'Last line comes after we win.']"

speaker: narrator
text: Tall tale 4: "There it is: the crack is under the third ring. Strike there and the whole thing goes." Nettle underlines it twice.

speaker: narrator
text: Pip fits the five clues into a spoon-shaped keyhole. A wall slides away: the SECRET ARMORY of the Spoon-Keepers!

speaker: narrator
text: Lore tablet: "MALTHRAX. Once court wizard of Emberhollow. Exiled for 'excessive candlelight'. Took it personally."

speaker: narrator
text: Sister Vey sinks beneath the water, her hymn ending in bubbles.

speaker: narrator
text: Mother Sporegrave collapses into a heap of harmless puffballs.

speaker: narrator
text: Skarn tumbles from the Broodmother's back. Among his things: Elowen's ribbon, and a map marked "B2".

speaker: narrator
text: Brambur pries his mother's hammer from Brakk's grip and weeps into his beard.

speaker: narrator
text: The moon rises over Emberhollow. A seal on the Blackspire cracks and breaks.

speaker: narrator
text: Scratched into the wall: "SKARN RIDES THE SPIDER QUEEN. THE RUSTY KEY OPENS HER DEN."

speaker: narrator
text: A faded mural shows a lizard as big as a cathedral. Someone has drawn a mustache on it.

speaker: narrator
text: A note: "Pip was here. Took spoon. Not sorry."

speaker: narrator
text: Dripping water spells nothing in particular. Brambur apologizes to it anyway.

speaker: narrator
text: An inscription: "BEYOND THE CORAL DOOR SLEEPS OLD CLUBTAIL. BRING SNACKS."

speaker: narrator
text: A cracked mirror. Professor Fizzwick spends some time admiring it.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystals here show your reflection a half-second late. Fizzwick waves at his. It waves back early.

speaker: narrator
text: Scratched in a crystal: "DO NOT LOOK THE LIZARD IN THE EYE. USE A MIRROR. a statue, probably"

speaker: narrator
text: A circle of mushrooms. Grumsh steps in it and refuses to say what he saw.

speaker: narrator
text: An anvil, still warm, with a smith's name scratched on it: "VARR".

speaker: narrator
text: A forge-mural: dwarves, a chimera, and a very small Brakk hiding behind it.

speaker: narrator
text: A sign: "BRAKK'S FORGE. NO REFUNDS. NO DWARVES. NO CHIMERA-PETTING."

speaker: narrator
text: Carved in gold: "HE WHO TAKES THE DAWNSTONE AMULET SHALL HOLD THE FIVE SEALS."

speaker: narrator
text: Enormous footprints. Fizzwick measures one. "Fizzwick estimates: large."

speaker: narrator
text: A shrine to a forgotten god of cutlery. Pip weeps openly.

speaker: narrator
text: Scratched into the stone: "The wardens fed the rats first, so the rats would learn to love the dark. They did."

speaker: narrator
text: A child's tally of days, 41 marks, then a drawing of a door.

speaker: narrator
text: A drowned scribe left a note: "The water was never a flood. It was a door the Tyrant wanted shut."

speaker: narrator
text: Pressed flowers, long dried: someone kept a garden down here.

speaker: narrator
text: Crystal-etched verse: "Glass remembers every face that looked into it. Do not look long."

speaker: narrator
text: A map fragment with a single mark: "The Warden sleeps standing."

speaker: narrator
text: Forge-script: "Every blade of Ashforge was quenched in a prisoner's name. Brakk kept the list."

speaker: narrator
text: A small hammer, wrapped in cloth. No name on it.

speaker: narrator
text: Carved over the lintel: "Gorvax was not the first thing to rule here. He is simply the loudest."

speaker: narrator
text: A saddle-strap, thunder-lizard hide. Someone rode these once.

speaker: narrator
text: Back in the Rat-Warrens. The scratching starts up again.

speaker: narrator
text: The Drowned Grotto. Cold water closes over your boots once more.

speaker: narrator
text: The Glimmerdeep hums its single note. Your reflections are waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ashforge heat greets you like an old, bad-tempered friend.

speaker: narrator
text: The Vault. The breathing has not stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: Here the rat-sign stops, as if even the vermin give this spot a wide berth. Something waits here that is not a rat.

speaker: narrator
text: Clear water bubbles from a cracked basin carved with a smiling face. It smells, astonishingly, of mint.

speaker: narrator
text: A spiral stair corkscrews down into the dark. A cold draught rises from it, carrying the smell of standing water.

speaker: narrator
text: The hidden passage is lined with tiny claw-marked tallies. Someone, or several someones, has been counting days here.

speaker: narrator
text: A low chamber stacked with mouldy grain sacks, every one of them gnawed open. The floor crunches underfoot, and you decide not to look down.

speaker: narrator
text: Dozens of tiny shrines line this room: thimbles, buttons and bent spoons arranged with real devotion around a portrait of a very fat rat.

speaker: narrator
text: Water pools in the middle of this chamber, and the walls are furred with nests of shredded cloth. The smell is magnificent, in the worst way.

speaker: narrator
text: Old smuggler's crates rot in the corners, stamped with the crest of Emberhollow. One still rattles faintly when you pass.

speaker: narrator
text: A ring of half-sunken lanterns marks this place, each one still somehow burning beneath the water.

speaker: narrator
text: A spring of warm, glowing water rises here, fizzing gently. The fungus around it grows in the shape of open hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Steps slick with algae lead down past a waterline carved with the warning "HIGH TIDE". The ink is fresh.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind the false wall is a dry pocket of air that smells of old parchment. Someone hid here while the water rose.

speaker: narrator
text: A flooded hall where bioluminescent eels drift between broken columns, lighting the water in slow blue pulses.

speaker: narrator
text: Shipwreck timbers jut from the walls of this cave, though the sea is miles away. A barnacled figurehead watches you pass.

speaker: narrator
text: Stalactites drip in this grotto like a broken water clock. The pools below are full of tiny white crabs that click in unison.

speaker: narrator
text: Nets heavy with old catches hang from the ceiling here. Some of the catches are wearing boots.

speaker: narrator
text: The hum of the crystals drops to a low, almost-words murmur here, as if the cavern is trying to tell you something.

speaker: narrator
text: A pool of liquid starlight shimmers in a crystal bowl. Drinking it tastes like the first cold breath of winter.

speaker: narrator
text: A crystal stair spirals downward, each step chiming a note as you test it. The tune is not a happy one.

speaker: narrator
text: The concealed grotto is dark: no crystals, no reflections, no hum. The silence is the loudest thing you have heard all day.

speaker: narrator
text: A gallery of statues frozen mid-stride, each one carrying a mirror that was raised a moment too late.

speaker: narrator
text: Huge amethyst columns split the light into slow purple rainbows. The floor is warm, and faintly ticks like cooling glass.

speaker: narrator
text: A garden of luminous mushrooms grows in a perfect spiral here. Stepping off the path makes them all turn to face you.

speaker: narrator
text: Shards of a shattered geode the size of a cottage litter this chamber, still humming with whatever broke out of it.

speaker: narrator
text: Here the hammer-song stops. Tools lie where they were dropped, mid-swing, and the air smells of a hasty departure.

speaker: narrator
text: Cool water pours from the mouth of a stone dwarf into a quenching trough. Steam curls up, smelling of iron and relief.

speaker: narrator
text: A brass-railed stair plunges into dark heat. Each step down is a little warmer, and the walls start to sweat.

speaker: narrator
text: A hidden smithy, its tools neatly hung and its coals banked as if the smith stepped out for lunch a hundred years ago.

speaker: narrator
text: A chamber of cooling moulds, each one shaped like a different weapon. Several of the moulds are empty and still warm.

speaker: narrator
text: Bellows the size of houses wheeze in this hall, pushed by nothing you can see. Embers dance in the draught.

speaker: narrator
text: An ore-cart track loops through this cavern, and a cart full of glowing slag still creaks slowly along it.

speaker: narrator
text: Racks of half-finished armour line the walls here, helmets turned so that every empty visor watches the door.

speaker: narrator
text: Old murals here show tiny heroes fleeing a towering lizard. The last panel has been scratched out with claws.

speaker: narrator
text: A basin of violet light pulses slowly, like a resting heartbeat. The pain of the road drains away as you drink.

speaker: narrator
text: Elowen's light pours from the altar ahead, golden and steady. Five keyholes wait around its rim.

speaker: narrator
text: This hidden alcove holds the bones of a knight in mirrored armour, one hand still pointing toward the vault.

speaker: narrator
text: Eggshells as big as barrels lie cracked open across this chamber. Whatever hatched has had a long time to grow.

speaker: narrator
text: Carved pillars of roaring lizards hold up a ceiling lost in darkness. Rain-sound echoes from far above, though there is no sky.

speaker: narrator
text: A trophy hall of crushed shields and bent swords, each tagged with a name in neat, patient handwriting.

speaker: narrator
text: The floor here is scorched in a long, perfect line, as if lightning once ran along it on four legs.

speaker: narrator
text: Emberhollow huddles in the long shadow of the Blackspire, a jumble of slate roofs and leaning chimneys. The square smells of woodsmoke and hot pies, and a bell tolls the hour a little nervously. Townsfolk hurry past, glancing at the dark tower the way you glance at a sleeping dog. Everyone here has lost someone to the maze.

speaker: narrator
text: The Boar & Spoon is warm, loud and smells of spilled ale, roast onions and wet dog. A fiddler saws at something cheerful in the corner while a mounted boar's head, wearing a spoon on a string, watches the door. Adventurers swap tall tales at long tables, and every one of them has a story about the Blackspire.

speaker: narrator
text: The Temple of Cant is cool and hushed, lit by tall candles that never quite drip. Incense of cedar and myrrh drifts past a donation box the size of a coffin. Somewhere a priest is counting coins very quietly.

speaker: narrator
text: Straw dummies hang from posts in the Training Grounds, most of them missing their heads. The air rings with clashing steel, barked orders and the thud of arrows striking targets. A grizzled sergeant watches you sideways and mutters something about soft hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Fizzbang's Trading Post is an avalanche of goods waiting to happen: ropes, lanterns, potions and at least one suspicious barrel. It smells of lamp oil and lavender soap. A gnome peers at you over a counter piled high with "bargains".

speaker: narrator
text: The cobbles end at a ring of standing stones around a gaping stair. Cold air breathes up from below, carrying faint echoes: a drip, a scratch, something like distant laughter. The town's last lantern swings above the entrance, and nobody has ever bothered to light it.

speaker: narrator
text: A woman crouches behind a toppled cheese barrel, bow half-drawn at a rat the size of a mastiff. Her braid is the colour of old copper and her smile is entirely too calm. "Don't mind me," she whispers. "Liora Wardenfall, of the Warden's Watch. I'm tracking my father, and this fellow is in the way."

speaker: narrator
text: The rat takes one look at the pair of you and flees, squeaking. Liora laughs and lowers her bow. "Twenty years I have walked these halls alone. Lead on, then."

speaker: narrator
text: "Aldous Wardenfall. The Watch's last Warden," she says, chewing. "I'll be at the Boar & Spoon when you want company. Ask for me, and I will come." (She is now in the Tavern's hire list.)

speaker: narrator
text: She tips two fingers to her brow. "You'll find me at the Boar & Spoon, if you change your mind."

speaker: narrator
text: Thimbles, buttons and a wedge of cheese the size of a wagon wheel ring a painted rat in a tiny crown. The rats around it have gone very quiet. All of them are looking at you.

speaker: narrator
text: The thimbles are heavy, bright gold. Somewhere inside the walls, a thousand tiny feet start moving.

speaker: narrator
text: You set a coin before the crown. The rats bow. Truly. The tunnels feel quieter.

speaker: narrator
text: It is alarmingly good cheese. Pip is moved to tears. Everyone feels rested and oddly proud.

speaker: narrator
text: A guardsman in a scorched Watch tabard sits wedged in a niche, sword across his knees. "Corporal Hale," he mumbles. "I ran. When the cultists came, I ran. I can't go back to the Captain. I can't."

speaker: narrator
text: "Thank you. I'll tell Rowan myself." He straightens a little, tabard and all. You feel like you did something that matters.

speaker: narrator
text: He closes his eyes and nods. "Fair." You note his name and leave him his sword. Duty is a heavy coat.

speaker: narrator
text: He hands over a battered pouch without meeting your eyes. It stings a little, taking it.

speaker: narrator
text: A bronze bell hangs half-sunk in a black pool, its rope trailing underwater. It tolls once, very softly, though nothing touched it.

speaker: narrator
text: Each toll rolls out across the water. Something far away answers, then thinks better of it. You feel rather wiser, and rather watched.

speaker: narrator
text: Cold hands find a clapper of pearl-white bone-metal. It hums in your palm: a fortune charm, still warm.

speaker: narrator
text: The water is deeper than it looks. You scramble out, coughing, with nothing but a bruise and a lesson.

speaker: narrator
text: The bell sighs out one last quiet note, as if relieved. Brambur prays for it.

speaker: narrator
text: A drowned ferryman sits in a rotted skiff, one dripping hand held out. "Thirty years I have waited for a fare," he says. "Pay, and I may finally sleep."

speaker: narrator
text: He bows. The skiff slides gently under the black water, and in the ripples lies a pearl the size of a plum.

speaker: narrator
text: The words come true and quiet. He sighs, smiles, and the skiff goes down with him. The tunnels feel safer.

speaker: narrator
text: He listens to the whole prayer, kindly. "A good try," he says. "I will wait a little longer." He gives you a nod.

speaker: narrator
text: You find a cache of waterlogged coins. The ferryman watches you without a word. It is somehow the worst part.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall crystal shows each of you as you truly are: braver, kinder and a little more frightened than you thought. It hums, waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: You each see what you are. Nobody speaks for a while, but everyone feels clearer. A strange new steadiness settles over the party.

speaker: narrator
text: The shards are worth a small fortune. The purse in your pocket feels suspiciously lighter afterwards.

speaker: narrator
text: The facets are tuned like a harp. You find a seam, and a small lens of mirror-glass comes away in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystal gives you a headache, and a very smug reflection of yourself. That is all.

speaker: narrator
text: A gnome with a lantern for a hat huddles in a crystal seam, sobbing into a pouch of glowing mushrooms. "Tobble Grindlewick!" he sniffles. "I sell glowcaps to the herbalist in Emberhollow! I got lost three days ago!"

speaker: narrator
text: It takes a while, and a little shouting. Tobble hugs your boots and runs for the surface. You feel good about it.

speaker: narrator
text: He eats everything, thanks you with enormous dignity, and gives you a bundle of the best glowcaps. "For the herbalist. Or you."

speaker: narrator
text: It is heavy and bright. He does not stop you. You realise a bit late that he is looking at you as if you were a monster.

speaker: narrator
text: An anvil older than the Forge stands in a ring of cold ash, a hammer laid across its face. Words are cut into the iron: STRIKE ONCE FOR STRENGTH. STRIKE TWICE FOR FEAR.

speaker: narrator
text: A single clear note rings out of the iron. Your hands steady, and the next chest you open will feel lucky.

speaker: narrator
text: The second ring is wrong: deep and hungry. It gives you something precious and takes something less visible. The dead stir in the walls.

speaker: narrator
text: You lay the hammer neatly across the anvil. A faint warmth follows you: respect, from something old. A flask of tempering oil appears at your feet.

speaker: narrator
text: A burned cultist foreman kneels beside a cooling channel, sobbing. "Mercy. I only held the keys. I never struck them. Let me go, and I will tell you where the smiths are held."

speaker: narrator
text: He gives you the keys and a hurried map of the lower forges. He bolts for the stairs, and a quiet nod from the party says you were right.

speaker: narrator
text: He swears on his mother, his mother's mother and the keys. He leaves, and you leave with his purse.

speaker: narrator
text: He laughs, hysterical, and darts away into the dark. The keys remain, but his promise does not.

speaker: narrator
text: It is quick and ugly. His keys are good keys, and his purse is heavy. Nobody says anything for a while.

speaker: narrator
text: A weathered statue of a Warden stands with open hands. At its feet a cracked plate reads: WHO KEEPS THE SEALS KEEPS THE TOWN. A faint horn-note hangs in the air.

speaker: narrator
text: The statue's hands close, just slightly, around yours. Warmth floods the party, and the hush of a good road settles around you.

speaker: narrator
text: Four voices, one oath. The statue's head tilts, almost fondly. The bond of the party tightens.

speaker: narrator
text: It comes away with a groan of old iron. Even as you lift it, you know the vault is going to remember this.

speaker: narrator
text: A cracked seal in the wall breathes a voice like warm oil. "Little knights. I can make you stronger. I ask only for a small favour."

speaker: narrator
text: Power pours into your hand. Something cold settles into your purse, and the dead begin to turn in their sleep.

speaker: narrator
text: The seal sputters, outraged. Nerves steady across the party, and the vault seems to wince.

speaker: serAldric
text: For the Dawn!

speaker: serAldric
text: Steel and faith!

speaker: serAldric
text: Stand and fall!

speaker: serAldric
text: I have taken worse.

speaker: serAldric
text: Hold the line!

speaker: serAldric
text: Not yet.

speaker: serAldric
text: Dawn guide my blade!

speaker: serAldric
text: Light, answer me!

speaker: serAldric
text: Rise, friend. We are not done.

speaker: serAldric
text: I feel the Dawn grow stronger.

speaker: serAldric
text: The way is clear. Onward.

speaker: serAldric
text: Tell Emberhollow... I tried.

speaker: serAldric
text: Rest while you can. I will keep watch.

speaker: serAldric
text: I cannot fall yet.

speaker: serAldric
text: Ser Aldric, at your service.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Take that!

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Come get some.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Out of my way.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Ugh. Is that all?

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: That one stung.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Hold still, you.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: That is how it is done!

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Whatever works.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Stop bleeding on my boots.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Still got some fight left.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Done. Who is buying?

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Bah... not like this.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: Fire, food, then sleep.

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: I am not dead yet!

speaker: vp_gruffwarrior
text: What now?

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Here I come!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Take this!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Let me through!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Ow! Okay, ow.

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: I am fine, I am fine!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Oh, so close!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Did you see that?!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Please work, please work!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Thank you, I needed that!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: I feel stronger already!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: We did it! We really did it!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: I am sorry... I tried.

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Can we tell stories by the fire?

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: I am not giving up!

speaker: vp_youngheroine
text: Ready when you are!

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Patience, then precision.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Be still.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Forgive me.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Old bones, young foes.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: A fair strike.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Age slows the hand.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Experience, young one.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Listen to the old words.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Be well, child.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Even now, I learn.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Another lesson, well taught.

speaker: vp_wiseelder

text: Sit. Let me tell you a story.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: I have seen worse days.

speaker: vp_wiseelder
text: Ah, you have need of me?

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Right behind you.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Nothing personal.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Surprise!

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Hey! Watch the face.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Lucky shot.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Slippery, aren't you?

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Straight between the ribs.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: A little trick of mine.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Nice. I owe you one.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Sharper every day.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Now, about that loot.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Well, that went badly.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Count the coins. Twice.

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: Time for a quiet exit!

speaker: vp_slyrogue
text: You rang?

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: In the name of the Crown!

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: Have at thee!

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: For honour!

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: A scratch. Nothing more.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: I shall not yield.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: Fortune, spare me.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: A blow worthy of a song!

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: By oath and light!

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: My gratitude, friend.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: I am worthy of the oath.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: Justice is served.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: My duty... is done.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: A knight sleeps lightly. Rest.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: I will stand to the last.

speaker: vp_nobleknight
text: At your command.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: For the shield wall!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Face me!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Break and bleed!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Is that your best?

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Pain is only a rumour.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Stand still, coward!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Valhalla sees that one!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Ancestors, lend me fire!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Good. Back to the fight.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: The gods smile on me.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Sing of this day!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Tell them... I fell fighting.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Sharpen steel. Drink deep.

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: I will die laughing!

speaker: vp_fierceshieldmaiden
text: Point me at them.

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: A little rhythm!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: And a one, and a two!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Encore!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Not the lute!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Ooh, that is a sour note.

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: I blame the audience.

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Take a bow, me!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Hit it, maestro!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: You are a lifesaver, truly!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: New verse, who dis?

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: That is a ballad, right there!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Remember my name... in song.

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Who wants a lullaby?

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: No no no, not the finale!

speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
text: Shall I play something?

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Hmph. Take it.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: By my beard.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Down you go.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Typical.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: I have had worse. Not much worse.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Of course I missed.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Well. That worked.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: I do not like magic. Fine.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Hm. Thank you, I suppose.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Better. Still gloomy, though.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: We lived. Do not celebrate.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: I knew it. I knew it.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: Cold stew. Lovely.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: This is how dwarves die.

speaker: vp_dourdwarf
text: What is it now?

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Be undone.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The stars command it.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Fade.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The veil trembles.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: You will regret that.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The threads slip.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Witness true power!

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Arcane winds, rise!

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Light mends all things.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The weave grows brighter.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: As the stars foretold.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The dark... takes me.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: The moon is kind tonight.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: My light is fading.

speaker: vp_mysticsorceress
text: Speak, and I shall listen.

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: RAAAGH!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: SMASH!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: COME ON, THEN!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: HA! TICKLES!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: Now I am angry!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: HOLD STILL!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: CRUSHED!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: Magic? Sure! BOOM!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: Aye, that is the stuff!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: I AM MIGHTIER!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: VICTORY! MORE ENEMIES!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: Tell my axe... I loved it.

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: MEAT! Where is the meat?

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: NOT YET! NOT YET!

speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
text: WHO NEEDS SMASHING?
